name: FindAI Credits
tagline: Discover AI free credits, startup deals, student offers, and exclusive software discounts

pricing.notes: The platform is free to browse. Revenue comes from affiliate partnerships and sponsored listings.

verdictSummary: Building a searchable AI deals directory is straightforward. The difficult part is continuously finding new offers, verifying them, preventing expired listings, ranking results, and growing enough SEO authority to make people discover it.
coreLoopDIY: Collect AI offers, store them in a database, categorize them, allow users to search and filter, and link users to claim the offers.
moatNotes: The software is easy to recreate. The real moat is maintaining an up-to-date database, ranking on Google, building relationships with AI companies, and becoming the default place users check before purchasing AI tools.
whyPeopleStillPay: Users don't pay for the directory itself. Companies pay because the platform brings qualified traffic and customers, while users save money and discover offers they would otherwise miss.

notes: Good example of a business where the code is easy but acquiring and maintaining high-quality data is the real challenge.
prompt:
Build me an AI software deals directory similar to FindAI Credits. Requirements:

- Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Supabase.
- Store offers with fields including company, title, description, category, offer value, eligibility, expiry date, affiliate link, logo, and verification status.
- Public pages should support search, filters, categories, and SEO-friendly dynamic routes.
- Generate Open Graph images, structured data, XML sitemap, RSS feed, and optimized metadata automatically.
- Build an admin dashboard for creating, editing, approving, and expiring deals.
- Add user accounts so users can bookmark offers and receive email notifications for new deals.
- Track clicks and basic analytics for every offer.
- Support featured listings and sponsored placements.
- Automatically detect expired offers and flag listings needing manual review.
- Everything should be responsive, fast, and optimized for Google indexing.
- Out of scope: existing affiliate partnerships, exclusive deals, proprietary data sources, established SEO rankings, and brand recognition. Those require ongoing business development rather than code.
- Include a README explaining the database schema, deployment to Vercel, SEO strategy, and content moderation workflow.
